label: Reference Pattern Library — filtered subset for consulting-pptx-skill's Production Integration v1
sourceNote: Trimmed copy of REFERENCE-PATTERN-LIBRARY-V0.1.2.json (an external, independently-developed Visual Planner / Reference Pattern Selector project), limited to the 3 families that project's own Selector Holdout rounds 2-3 scored 10/10 with zero wrong selections: matrix, hierarchy, roadmap-phaseband. Fields specific to that project's own golden-fixtures/renderer (groundedIn, revisionNote, referenceAssets, evidenceStatus, renderability, referenceLocator) are dropped — they describe evidence and renderability against THAT project's render.js, not this one. What's kept is the semantic ELIGIBILITY CONTRACT (useWhen/requiredSemanticRoles/relationshipsRequired/doNotUseWhen/etc) each pattern's own spec explicitly scopes as Pattern-Selector-owned, independent of which renderer ultimately draws it. See pipeline/scripts/pre_family_ir_to_slide_spec.mjs for how a selected pattern here maps onto this project's own SlideSpec templates (matrix_2x2/issue_tree/gantt).

patterns.name: Matrix Hero (Priority Matrix, rich)
patterns.useWhen: 2 genuinely authored axes (not just 4 box-shaped items) AND at least one quadrant carries more than a single-sentence description — priorityLabel + title + body [+ evidence] authored per quadrant, not merely a label.
requiredSemanticRoles: label or title per populated quadrant
relationshipsRequired: axis_membership (>=1 per quadrant group, covering 2 distinct axis elements for at least 3 of the 4 possible quadrant groupIds)
patterns.emphasisModel: 0 or 1 quadrant may carry element.emphasis=true (an authored flag, never inferred from which quadrant 'sounds' most important).
patterns.supportingBand: none — matrix's own quadrant structure already carries the 'so what' per zone.
doNotUseWhen: only 1 axis is authored, or axis words describe the SAME dimension twice
4 box-shaped items exist but no 2-axis judgment criteria are ever articulated anywhere in the content — use cards instead
quadrant content is a single plain sentence with no priorityLabel/body richness — use RP-MATRIX-PLAIN-01 instead

patterns.name: Priority Matrix (plain / badge tier)
patterns.useWhen: 2 genuinely authored axes, but each quadrant is a single descriptive sentence — no separate priorityLabel/title/body/evidence fields authored per quadrant.
requiredSemanticRoles: label per populated quadrant (the single sentence)
optionalSemanticRoles: a short priority badge per quadrant (最優先/高/中/低)
patterns.emphasisModel: same as RP-MATRIX-HERO-01 — 0 or 1 quadrant may carry an authored emphasis flag.
patterns.doNotUseWhen: same near-miss boundary as RP-MATRIX-HERO-01. If richer per-quadrant fields ARE authored, use RP-MATRIX-HERO-01 instead — variant choice is purely about which fields were authored, not a quality judgment.

patterns.name: Workstream Hierarchy
patterns.useWhen: an authored root node (a named top-level owner/committee) with >=2 child nodes explicitly reporting to it.
optionalSemanticRoles: bullets or body per child (role/responsibility list)
relationshipsRequired: contains (root -> each child, at least 2 edges)
patterns.densityRange: low to medium, depends on child count and per-child detail
patterns.emphasisModel: no structural emphasis mechanism for this family yet — emphasis should stay empty.
patterns.doNotUseWhen: content has only a shared section heading over a flat list, with NO authored root/ownership relationship at all — use cards instead.

patterns.name: PMI Roadmap (phase-banded)
patterns.useWhen: milestones are grouped under authored phase objects (each phase has its own title/description) AND at least one milestone carries an authored emphasis marker.
optionalSemanticRoles: a slide-level closing/outcomes group distinct from any single phase or milestone
patterns.densityRange: medium — roadmap-phaseband's richness comes from phase/milestone COUNT more than field count
patterns.emphasisModel: milestone-level authored flag — exactly 1 milestone is typically emphasized.
patterns.supportingBand: often present — a slide-level closing takeaways group distinct from any individual phase or milestone.
patterns.doNotUseWhen: milestones exist but are NOT grouped under authored phase objects (no contains edges) — use the plain 'roadmap' template's flat `sections` shape instead.

patterns.name: Executive KPI Dashboard
patterns.groundedIn: pipeline/reference-patterns/golden-fixtures-v0.2/RP-KPI-EXEC-DASHBOARD-01.jpg — Library v0.2, first pattern implemented (not part of the external Visual Planner project's own library; independently defined for this project).
patterns.useWhen: 3-5 KPIs, each with an authored label+value, numbers-as-the-main-content (not explanatory prose), and the slide's purpose is a summary/performance-snapshot/executive overview — not a single hero metric, not a dense 6+ metric table, and not primarily a time-series or item-comparison story.
requiredSemanticRoles: title (KPI label) + value (KPI number) per KPI, 3-5 KPIs
optionalSemanticRoles: body (driver/context note) and context (subtitle) per KPI
icon (bar-chart/coins/pie/cycle) and spark (comma-separated mini-history) per KPI
a slide-level headline (groupId=null) as the key-message band above the KPI row
an insights group (bullets, bordered panel) and/or a trendChart group (1-2 bar series + an optional line series on its own scale) below the KPI row
patterns.emphasisModel: no structural emphasis mechanism for this family — KPI values speak for themselves; don't author emphasis here.
patterns.supportingBand: optional — an insights list and/or a trend chart below the KPI row, distinct from any single KPI tile.
doNotUseWhen: only 1 KPI is authored — use a hero-KPI-shaped template instead
6+ KPIs are authored — this becomes a dense dashboard/table, not this pattern
explanatory prose is the main content and numbers are incidental — use cards instead
the point is a time-series comparison across many periods — use a chart template instead
the point is comparing named items/options against each other — use RP-COMPARISON-TABLE-01 instead

patterns.name: Comparison Table
patterns.groundedIn: pipeline/reference-patterns/golden-fixtures-v0.2/RP-COMPARISON-TABLE-01.jpg — Library v0.2, second pattern implemented (independently defined for this project, not part of the external Visual Planner project's own library). The existing comparison_table template already had a 2-candidate + per-row-implication flat shape (proven in the M&A investment-committee deck) — this pattern adds a second, richer shape (N candidates x criteria grid + a side 総括 summary panel) rather than replacing it.
patterns.useWhen: 2-5 named candidates/options are evaluated against a SHARED set of qualitative criteria (not raw numeric comparison), each cell rated on a closed ◎/○/△/× scale with a short caption — and the slide's point is which candidate to pick, not a per-criterion narrative implication.
requiredSemanticRoles: title (candidate label) + value (rated cell, one per criterion) per candidate, 2-5 candidates
optionalSemanticRoles: emphasis=true on a candidate's title element to highlight that column as the leading option
a recommendation group (title = row label, one value cell per candidate) as a bottom summary row inside the table itself
a slide-level comparisonSummary panel beside the table: numbered points + a highlighted conclusion sentence
patterns.emphasisModel: at most 1 candidate column may be highlighted (authored, never inferred from which column 'looks' best).
patterns.supportingBand: optional — the comparisonSummary panel (総括 + 結論), distinct from any single cell.
doNotUseWhen: only 1 candidate exists — there is nothing to compare
6+ candidates — this becomes a dense table, not this pattern
cell content is raw comparable numbers rather than a qualitative rating — a chart or a plain data table is more honest
the point is a per-criterion narrative read-out for exactly 自社 vs 他社 — the existing flat table/headers shape (criterion+company+competitor+implication) already covers that case and stays supported

patterns.name: Decision Ask
patterns.groundedIn: pipeline/reference-patterns/golden-fixtures-v0.2/RP-DECISION-ASK-01.jpg — Library v0.2, third pattern implemented (independently defined for this project). The existing decision_page template's flat shape (a single ask + a plain numbered decisions[] list) is unchanged — this pattern is a second, richer shape (N decision columns, each with its own numbered header/context/icon/title/actions) plus an optional bottom recommendation + next-steps bar.
patterns.useWhen: 2-4 distinct approval/judgment items are being put to a decision-making body in one sitting, each with its own concrete follow-up action(s) — the slide's primary purpose is obtaining a decision, not summarizing conclusions or comparing options.
patterns.canonicalVariant: 3 decision groups + a recommendation + nextSteps — this is the exact composition of the reference image and the fixture verified closest to it (visual fidelity reviewed and accepted at this level of match). 2 and 4 decision groups, and omitting recommendation/nextSteps, are supported ADAPTIVE variants for when the real content genuinely has 2 or 4 items — not a substitute for authoring the canonical shape when 3 items with a recommendation legitimately fit.
requiredSemanticRoles: number + title + bullets (>=1 action) per decision group, 2-4 groups
optionalSemanticRoles: context (a 1-2 line framing sentence above the title) and icon (org-chart/bar-chart/people) per decision group

a recommendation group (title = tag label defaulting to "推奨", body = the recommendation sentence) as a highlighted chevron bar below the columns — present in the canonical variant, optional in adaptive variants
a nextSteps group (bullets, order preserved) as a numbered sequence beside the recommendation bar — present in the canonical variant, optional in adaptive variants
patterns.emphasisModel: no structural emphasis mechanism for this family — every decision column is equally a decision to be made; don't author emphasis here.
patterns.supportingBand: optional — the recommendation + nextSteps bar, distinct from any single decision column.
doNotUseWhen: the slide is a plain conclusion recap with no decision being requested — use RP-KEY-TAKEAWAYS-01 instead
the point is choosing between named options — use RP-COMPARISON-TABLE-01 instead
the point is a multi-week/multi-day execution timeline — use the roadmap/100-Day patterns instead
the columns are explanatory, not decision items (no concrete action being asked for) — use plain cards instead

patterns.name: Key Takeaways
patterns.groundedIn: pipeline/reference-patterns/golden-fixtures-v0.2/RP-KEY-TAKEAWAYS-01.jpg — Library v0.2, fourth pattern implemented (independently defined for this project). The existing recommendation_pillars template's flat shape (a plain sections[] list: number circle + title + copy + bullets) is unchanged — this pattern is a second, richer shape mandating the reference image's full 3-part composition (takeaway columns + a right insight-synthesis panel + a bottom So What conclusion bar), not just the column cards alone.
patterns.useWhen: the slide's job is to synthesize a body of analysis into a small number of headline conclusions AND connect them to concrete implications AND state the resulting so-what in one sentence — all three layers together, not a conclusion recap alone.
patterns.canonicalVariant: 3 takeaway columns + an insightPanel (3 items) + soWhat — the reference image's own composition. 2 and 4 takeaway columns are supported ADAPTIVE variants (same precedent as RP-DECISION-ASK-01); unlike decision_page's recommendation/nextSteps, insightPanel and soWhat are NEVER optional here at any column count — omitting either degrades this into 3 plain cards, which already has its own simpler template (the existing flat `sections` shape).
requiredSemanticRoles: number + category + headline + body (supportText) per takeaway, 2-4 takeaways
an insightPanel group with >=1 item sub-group, each with number + title + body
a soWhat group with a body (the so-what sentence)
optionalSemanticRoles: a title on the insightPanel group (panel heading, defaults to "示唆")
a title on the soWhat group (tag label, defaults to "So What")
patterns.emphasisModel: no structural emphasis mechanism for this family — every takeaway is equally a headline conclusion; don't author emphasis here.
patterns.supportingBand: mandatory — the insightPanel + soWhat bar are load-bearing parts of this pattern's own definition, not an optional add-on the way other patterns' supporting bands are.
doNotUseWhen: there is no synthesized so-what, only a list of findings — use plain cards or the flat recommendation_pillars shape instead
a decision is actually being requested, not just conclusions reported — use RP-DECISION-ASK-01 instead
the point is comparing named options — use RP-COMPARISON-TABLE-01 instead
